question_text: Construct count_above(node, limit) in Python for a singly linked list. node is the current node or None; each node has next and customer.budget. Return the number of customers whose budget is strictly greater than limit. Use simple nonbranching recursion.
adaptation_rationale: Retains nonbranching recursive conditional count; node traversal avoids importing JavaLinkedList indexed access costs/API.

marking_points.criterion: Makes one recursive call progressing to node.next.
Compares the current budget with limit using strict greater-than.
Adds 1 to the recursive result exactly when the budget qualifies.
Returns the unchanged recursive result otherwise.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent technically correct wording or valid implementation earning the specified independent points.
partial_credit_notes: Award each stated point independently up to the total; do not double-credit the same idea.

verification.technical: Concrete marking points independently reasoned from the defined context and exact 2027 scope.
verification.code_check: Executable checks saved under checks/ where applicable.

test_code:
from types import SimpleNamespace
head=None
for budget in [5000,3000,4000]:head=SimpleNamespace(customer=SimpleNamespace(budget=budget),next=head)
assert count_above(head,3000)==2
assert count_above(head,5000)==0
assert count_above(None,3000)==0
